relevance_reason: Reports the index consanguineous family with unclassified OFDS with short stature and brachymesophalangia caused by homozygous IFT57 splice mutation, with functional studies — defines OFD18.

findings.statement: Thevenon et al. (2016) described an unclassified type of oral-facial-digital syndrome (OFDS) with short stature and brachymesophalangia, overlapping with Ellis-van Creveld syndrome (EVCS), caused by a homozygous hypomorphic mutation in IFT57, representing the first description of a ciliary transport defect in OFDS.
quotes: Here, we report on a unique consanguineous family with an unclassified type of OFDS with short stature and brachymesophalangia overlapping with EVCS, and caused by a homozygous hypomorphic mutation of IFT57, affecting splicing and altering protein function.
This report identifies the implication of IFT57 in human pathology and highlights the first description of a ciliary transport defect in OFDS

findings.statement: Thevenon et al. (2016) restudied a consanguineous family, previously reported by Phadke et al. (1999), with 3 affected sibs, followed up for 15 years; one sib (II-3) died at 17 years of a complicated pulmonary infection. Subject II-1, a male examined at 25 years, had normal intelligence, short stature (155 cm, -3 SD), square face with short forehead, upslanting palpebral fissures, high nasal bridge, pyriform nose, short philtrum, medial cleft of upper lip, supernumerary frenulae, missing incisors, pronounced brachydactyly, upper limb postaxial polydactyly, and preaxial polydactyly of the feet due to first metatarsal duplication; x-rays showed severe mesophalangeal shortening, short femoral necks with varus femurs, and genu valgum, with no thoracic deformity or vertebral anomalies; heart, renal, and abdominal ultrasounds were normal.
quotes: The reported subjects born to healthy consanguineous parents (Figure 1A) were first published during childhood and followed up for 15 years. Subject II-3 died at 17 years of age because of a complicated pulmonary infection.

He had short stature with a final height of 155 cm (−3 SD), weight 45 kg (<−3 SD) and occipito-frontal circumference (OFC) 50 cm (mean). The clinical examination showed a square face with short forehead, upslanting palpebral fissures, high nasal bridge with pyriform nose above a short philtrum and a medial clefting of upper lip (Figure 1B).

X-rays of the hands and feet showed severe mesophalangeal shortening. Pre-axial polydactyly was diagnosed, because of first metatarsal duplication. Bone studies showed bilateral short femoral necks with varus femurs, symmetric genu valgus and no vertebral anomalies.

findings.statement: Thevenon et al. (2016) described subject II-2, a female examined at 22 years with normal intelligence and short stature (122 cm, -5 SD), square face, narrow forehead, enophthalmos, upslanting palpebral fissures, broad nasal bridge, bilateral hypopigmented pseudoclefts, medial labial cleft, missing incisors, supernumerary frenulae, marked brachydactyly, and 4-limb postaxial polydactyly. X-rays showed mesophalangeal shortening, fused proximal phalanges and bifid distal phalanges, first metatarsal duplication with absent middle phalanges (preaxial polydactyly), vertebral bodies with medial notches without platyspondyly, bilateral cervical ribs, gracile long bones, and short femoral necks; there was no thoracic deformity, and brain MRI and abdominal and heart ultrasounds were normal.
quotes: She had short stature with a final height of 122 cm (−5 SD), weight 37 kg (−2 SD) and a conserved OFC at 51 cm (mean). Clinical examination showed a square face with narrow forehead, enophtalmia with up-slanting palpebral fissures, broad nasal bridge.
Digital anomalies included marked brachydactyly, four-limb post-axial polydactyly, surgically removed during infancy. There was neither thoracic deformity, nor dolichostenomelia.

Abnormal vertebral bodies with medial notches but no platyspondyly, bilateral cervical ribs without narrow thorax were also present. Long bones were gracile with shortened femoral neck. Brain MRI, abdominal and heart ultrasounds were normal.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Partial duplication of the distal phalanges of the hand

findings.statement: Thevenon et al. (2016) concluded on review that the family had an unclassified OFDS type with skeletal dysplasia rather than EVCS, since patients lacked rib shortening or thoracic narrowing but had short stature, brachymesophalangia, and stocky femoral necks. The affected individuals had no visual complaints, although retinopathy was not excluded.
quotes: Indeed, the reported subjects did not present rib shortening or thorax narrowness/deformity, but displayed a short stature, brachymesophalangia and stocky femoral necks, which suggests a new OFDS subtype with skeletal dysplasia.
However, these three individuals did not have visual complaints and there was no exclusion of ophthalmological involvement such as a retinopathy.

findings.statement: Thevenon et al. (2016) performed homozygosity mapping in 2 affected sibs of the consanguineous family and identified shared runs of homozygosity totaling 11 Mb on chromosome 3 (chr3:104822019-111671862) and chromosome 10 (chr10:1372501-6029726); the chromosome 10 interval was excluded by segregation in the third sib.
quotes: This approach identified 11-megabase of shared runs of homozygosity spreading from chr3:104822019-111671862 and chr10:1372501-6029726 (Hg19) (Figure 2A).
Extended familial segregation with Sanger sequencing in Subject 3 excluded one of the 2 homozygous interval

findings.statement: In 3 sibs from a consanguineous family with an unclassified OFDS with short stature and brachymesophalangia, Thevenon et al. (2016) identified by homozygosity mapping and exome sequencing a homozygous synonymous variant in the IFT57 gene (c.777G>A, p.Lys259Lys; NM_018010.3) affecting the last base of exon 6. Sanger sequencing confirmed homozygosity in all 3 affected sibs; the variant was absent from ExAC and from 50 healthy northern Indian controls. In patient fibroblasts it caused a complex splicing pattern with normal transcript plus 3 aberrant transcripts (in-frame skipping of exon 6, in-frame skipping of exons 5-6, and out-of-frame skipping of exons 4-6) detected only after NMD inhibition, with reduced IFT57 mRNA, consistent with a hypomorphic allele.
quotes: namely an IFT57 synonymous variation (chr3:g.107910368C>T, c.777G>A, p.Lys259Lys, RefSeq accession number NM_018010.3). This variant was absent from the ExAC database
Sanger sequencing confirmed the variation at a homozygous status in the 3 affected subjects.

The c.777G>A substitution affecting the last base of exon 6 induces a complex splicing pattern including the normal transcript (A) but also three pathological mRNAs resulting from exon(s) skipping (B, C, and D). The pathological transcripts are only detected after inhibition of the NMD pathway.

findings.statement: Thevenon et al. (2016) found no causative IFT57 mutations by Sanger sequencing in 13 OFDS patients (with polydactyly and cleft lip/palate) and 12 EVCS patients negative for EVC/EVC2, and no biallelic causative mutations in exome or ciliome data from 172 patients with various ciliopathies.
quotes: Sanger sequencing for the 11 coding exon and intron boundaries of IFT57 was performed on 25 OFDS and EVCS subjects. No causative mutation was identified. Exome or ciliome data from 172 subjects with various ciliopathy phenotypes did not identify any biallelic causative mutations.

findings.statement: Thevenon et al. (2016) found that patient fibroblasts had normal primary cilia number and length but decreased anterograde ciliary transport, with IFT57 staining at the ciliary tip significantly decreased (90% vs 35%) and increased at the basal body. SAG stimulation produced poor induction of GLI1 mRNA in patient fibroblasts, and siRNA knockdown of IFT57 in control fibroblasts abolished GLI1 induction, indicating defective sonic hedgehog signaling; the authors suggested defective hedgehog signaling underlies many of the phenotypes.
quotes: Primary cilia number and length in fibroblasts from the subject with the IFT57 mutation were similar to those in controls (Figure 3A and B).

In the subject’s fibroblasts, staining of the ciliary tip with IFT57 was significantly decreased (90% versus 35%; p<0.001) while staining of the basal body of the primary cilium was significantly increased (p<0.01).

A 3.7 fold increase in GLI1 transcript expression was observed in siRNA control-transfected cells after 30 hours in the presence of SAG (Figure 3C) whereas no induction of Gli1 mRNA expression was observed in siRNA IFT57-transfected cells.

relevance_reason: The paper reports a consanguineous family with a new OFD variant that has acromelic short stature, which fits the OFD18 phenotype.

findings.statement: Phadke et al. (1999) reported a consanguineous family in which sibs had a new variety of oral-facial-digital syndrome. Along with oral, facial, and digital malformations, the sibs had acromelic short stature and genu valgum. The authors noted that these features overlap with Ellis-van Creveld syndrome. One sib also had urinary incontinence and growth hormone deficiency, which the authors said had not been reported before in any type of OFDS.
quotes: Here, we report a consanguineous family with a new variety of OFDS associated with acromelic short stature and genu valgum; the features overlapping with Ellis Van Creveld syndrome.
One of the sibs has urinary incontinence and growth hormone deficiency, which has not been reported earlier in any type of OFDS in the literature.

findings.statement: Phadke et al. (1999) described this OFDS variant in sibs born to consanguineous parents.
